newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/April OEX calls draw speculators.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/April OEX calls draw speculators.

text.p: Volume in April S&P100 index calls ballooned as speculators bet the stock market rally would outpace the soon-expiring Aprils' steep time-decay and a softening in implied volatilities, traders said.

Open interest in at-the-money April contracts, which expire on Friday, was in many cases still increasing, while volume in May stayed relatively subdued, reflecting a negligible pickup in rollovers, they said.
"My guess is that people are buying these things for directional trades," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"It would be interesting to see if this thing holds this afternoon," he said.
OEX was up 4.17 points at 746.55 at 1115 CDT/1615 GMT.

The at-the-money April 745 calls, whose open interest actually increased by 630 to 13,917 contracts on Wednesday, and 750 calls had volume of more than 13,000 contracts each by 1100 CDT/1600 GMT -- by far the most actively traded OEX options.

The 745 and 750 strikes were sucking in most of the speculative interest because out-of-the-money Aprils were becoming hopelessly low-delta contracts that did not have enough gamma to beat time decay ahead of expiration.
With softer implied volatilities resulting from handsome gains in the OEX this week also weighing heavily, premiums on April 560 calls were down despite a four-point rally in OEX today, for instance.
CBOE volatility index was off 0.11 point to 20.38 at 1120 CDT/1620 GMT.
Traders said they were skeptical how long the rally, which followed heavy losses since the March 25 Federal Reserve credit tightening and climaxed last Friday, could last.
"There is a bullish bias during the expiration week," said Tim Ord of analytical publication Ord Oracle.
He noted that the market could start deteriorating once the expiration week was over.
He said Friday's bottom was not significant enough to end a downtrend, adding that New York Stock Exchange volume on Friday and Monday was in the low 400 million share area.
"That's pretty low (volume) for a panic low," Ord said.

He also noted that there had not been enough strong down readings in NYSE tick index during the bottoming process. The tick index today ranged from minus 47 to plus 644, and Ord said the relatively high uptick reading was a bearish signal.
On the other hand, some traders saw positive signals in today's rebound in the technology sector, which had been sliding this week despite the strong rally in blue-chip stocks in broader areas.
The Nasdaq 100 index was up 13.59 at 812.24 at 1135 CDT/1635 GMT, with good volume in CBOE's NDX calls with strike prices from 800 to 830.
Traders said Microsoft Corp's quarterly earnings results due out later in the day might be critical in maintaining the sector's early strength.
